name: Warmth Index
description: Vantablack Media's highest-grossing release of the 2210s — a disaster epic in which a cascading Great Lakes thermal collapse threatens to render GLMZ uninhabitable within 72 hours, and a team of Tier 2-4 specialists from wildly different backgrounds must cooperate across sector boundaries to prevent it. The neural-feed experience allows viewers to switch between three protagonists at will, each offering a radically different sensory and social experience of the same crisis. The film is technically flawless and emotionally engineered with precision.
cultural_impact: Briefly unified public discourse across tier lines and is credited with generating enough political pressure to pass the 2219 Lake Compact environmental protections, though cynics argue Vantablack engineered that outcome deliberately.
story_hooks: The thermal collapse scenario is not fictional — someone inside Vantablack used the film's production as cover to model and test an actual attack on the lake system.
The film's three-protagonist switching mechanic was used to harvest comparative emotional response data from millions of viewers; someone wants that data.
A Tier 1 Shelf community that would have been the first casualty of the depicted collapse was never mentioned in the film — and their exclusion was intentional.
